A finite-state abstraction (state in Fin S -> Fin (poly N)) cannot hold real scalars exactly and ignores workspace. A real-valued word model with arbitrary transition maps makes the space bound vacuous, since one real encodes unbounded information. Each item needs a joint probability space shared with the learner's own randomness and a definition of components as online processes whose state depends only on past losses. (iii) The conclusion has nested asymptotics: an existential fixed polynomial p, 'sufficiently large n,T', O-tilde hiding fixed log powers, and an omega(1) exponent quantified uniformly over the family. Any Lean rendering would rest on modeling choices (word contents, workspace accounting, how the component's randomness is coupled with the learner's) that either trivialize the claim or depart materially from the paper.
